sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Reference Gas**: **CO2** is the baseline with a GWP of 1. All other gases are measured relative to it.
• **Time Horizon**: GWP is typically calculated over **20, 100, or 500 years**. The **100-year GWP (GWP100)** is the standard metric used in international climate policy (e.g., IPCC reports).
• **Radiative Efficiency**: The ability of a gas to absorb infrared radiation per unit mass.
• **Atmospheric Lifetime**: The duration a gas remains in the atmosphere before being removed by chemical or physical processes.

items.definition: The change in the net downward minus upward radiative flux at the tropopause; GWP is the time-integrated radiative forcing.
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change periodically updates GWP values in its Assessment Reports, which countries use for their National Greenhouse Gas Inventories.

items.title: Major Applications & Policy
items.content:
• **Carbon Footprinting**: Converting diverse GHG emissions into 'CO2 equivalent' (CO2e) units.
• **Kyoto Protocol**: Used GWP values from the IPCC Second Assessment Report (SAR) for compliance.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Short-lived Climate Pollutants (SLCPs)**: GWP100 underestimates the impact of short-lived gases like Methane.
• **GWP* (GWP-star)**: A newer metric proposed to better reflect the warming impact of short-lived gases.

items.title: Mnemonic for GWP Intensity
items.content:
• **Phrase**: 'Super Methane Nitrous Carbon'
• **Decoded**: SF6 (Super) > N2O (Nitrous) > CH4 (Methane) > CO2 (Carbon). This helps rank gases by their warming potential.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Atmospheric Lifetime' with 'GWP'. A gas can have a short lifetime (Methane) but a very high GWP due to high radiative efficiency.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'CO2-equivalent (CO2e)' when discussing India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to demonstrate technical depth.

keyTakeaways: GWP is a relative, not absolute, measure of warming potential.
The 100-year time horizon is the standard for international climate reporting.
GWP values are updated by the IPCC; always check if the question refers to a specific Assessment Report.
